issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting specifications for the Farm.animals attribute: the UML diagram declares animals as a List<Animal>, while the textual Part 3 instructs implementing the aggregation using a Set (HashSet) to ensure uniqueness. The provided solution implements animals as a List<Animal>, which contradicts the textual requirement to use a Set and the uniqueness constraint. This ambiguity can confuse students about whether duplicates are allowed and which collection type to use, and it may cause mismatches with tests or grading expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction by choosing one collection type and making all artifacts consistent. Preferred fix: update the UML and any examples to specify animals: Set<Animal> and change the solution (and template hints) to use private Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>(); with corresponding getter/setter and iteration. Alternatively, if List semantics are intended, update the textual Part 3 to remove the requirement for a Set/HashSet and state that a List is used (and remove the uniqueness requirement). Ensure tests and sample code match the chosen design.
